FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
and Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division 
Council. 


Fipronil granules are generally used as an insecticide. Fipronil granules are generally manufactured to contain 
0.3 percent (m/m) of fipronil. 


In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 
and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides 
Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding-off numerical values (revised) . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16331 : 2015 


Indian Standard 
FIPRONIL GRANULES — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for Fipronil granules. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below: 


IS No. Title 
460 (Part 1): Specification for test sieves: Part 1 


1985 Wire cloth test sieves (third revision) 

1070 : 1992 Reagent grade water — Specification 
(third revision) 

6940 : 1982 Methods of test for pesticides and 


their formulations (first revision) 


8190 (Part 1): Requirement for packing of 


1988 pesticides: Part 1 Solid pesticides 
(second revision) 
10627 : 1983 Methods of sampling of pesticidal 
formulations 
3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Constituents 


3.1.1 The material shall consist of Fipronil technical 
as active ingredient impregnated on suitable carrier(s) 
together with binder(s), stabilizer(s) and/or other 
formulant(s). The granules may or may not contain 
colouring agents. 


3.1.2 Fipronil technical shall be employed in the 
formulation of the material. 


3.2 Physical 


The material shall comply with the physical 
requirements specified in 3.2.1 to 3.2.5. 


3.2.1 Description 


The product shall consist of dry, free flowing granules, 
free from visible extraneous matter and dust except 
for the amount specified (see 3.2.3). It may contain 
added colouring agents. 


3.2.2 Sieving Requirements 


Not less than 97 percent by mass of the product shall 
pass through a test sieve having a mesh size of upper 
declared limit and not more than 5 percent by mass of 
the product shall pass through a test sieve having a 
mesh size of lower declared limit when determined by 
the method described in 12.1 of IS 6940. 


3.2.2.1 The ratio of lower to upper limit of the sieve 
sizes given under 3.2.2 shall not exceed 1 : 3. 


3.2.3 Dust 


When determined by the method prescribed in 12.1 of 
IS 6940, not more than 1.0 percent by mass of the 
product shall pass through 75 micron IS Sieve [see 
IS 460 (Part 1)]. 


3.2.3.1 The portion passing through this sieve shall 
contain fipronil 0.270 - 0.360 percent by mass when 
determined by method described in Annex A. 


3.2.4 Moisture Content 


When determined by the method described in 4 of 
IS 6940, the moisture content shall not exceed 
1.0 percent by mass. 


3.3 Chemical 


The material shall comply with the chemical 
requirements specified in 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


3.3.1 Fipronil Content 


When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex A, the observed fipronil content percent (m/m) 
of any of the samples shall not differ from the declared 
nominal value by more than the percent tolerance limits 
given below: 


Nominal Value Tolerance Limits 


Percent Percent 
Up to 9 +10 
—5 
of the nominal 
Above 9 and below 50 +5 value 
50 and above +5 


-3 
3.3.2 Acidity/Alkalinity 


When tested by the method prescribed in 13.5 of 
IS 6940, the acidity (as H,SO,) shall not be more than 


IS 16331 : 2015 


0.1 percent by mass or alkalinity (as NaOH) of the 
material shall not be more than 0.15 percent by mass. 


4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in polyethylene pouches/ 
containers. The packing shall also meet the general 
requirements given in IS 8190 (Part 1). 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The containers shall be securely closed and the 
following information shall be marked legibly and 
indelibly on each container in addition to any other 
information, as is necessary under the Insecticides Act, 
1968 and Rules framed thereunder: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 
c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal fipronil content, percent (m/m); 


h) Cautionary notice worded as in the 
Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed 
thereunder; and 


j) Any other information required under the 
Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark 


5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 


provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


6 SAMPLING 


When freshly manufactured material in bulk quantity 
and/or the retail pack of the formulated product is/are 
offered for inspection, representative sample of the 
material shall be drawn and tested as prescribed 
in IS 10627, and if tested within 90 days of its date of 
manufacture, the criteria for conformity shall be that 
the contents in percent (m/m), shall not be less than 
the declared nominal value. The upper limit for 
conformity shall be the same as those given in 3.3.1. 


When the material is offered for inspection after 90 
days of its manufacture, sampling shall be done as 
prescribed in IS 10627. However, the criteria for 
conformity of the material, when tested, shall be the 
limits of tolerances, as applicable over the declared 
nominal value, and given under 3.3.1. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the appropriate 
methods referred to in 3.2.1 to 3.2.4, 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in the 
tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 16331 : 2015 


ANNEX A 
(Clause 3.3.1) 
DETERMINATION OF FIPRONIL CONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


The fipronil content is determined by high performance 
liquid chromatography (HPLC) equipped with UV 
detector using external standard technique. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 A high performance liquid chromatography 
system equipped with ultraviolet detector and 
chromatographic software/printer plotter-cum- 
integrator or PC based data system is used for this 
determination. The suggested operative parameters are 
as follows, but can be changed if necessary, provided 
standardization is done: 


Column : Stainless steel, 25 cm x 4.6 mm 
i.d., packed with C 18, 5 um 

Temperature : Ambient 

Mobile phase : Acetonitrile : Water (70 : 30 v/v) 

Flow rate 1.0 ml/min 

Injection volume : 20 ul 


Detector : Ultraviolet detector (280 nm) 


A typical HPLC chromatogram of fipronil technical is 
given in Fig. 1. 


A-2.2 Analytical Balance 

A-2.3 Microlitre Syringe — 25 ul capacity. 
A-2.3 Magnetic Stirrer 

A-2.4 Ultrasonic Bath 

A-2.5 Standard Glassware 


A-3 REAGENTS 


A-3.1 Fipronil Reference Standard, of known purity. 


4.895 — 


Figrontt 


A-3.2 Acetonitrile — AR grade, or equivalent. 
A-3.3 Water — AR grade, or equivalent. 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Preparation of Mobile Phase 


Mix acetonitrile and water in the proportion of 70 : 30 
(v/v) and pass through membrane filter under vacuum. 
Homogenize the mixture using a magnetic stirrer and 
allow to attain room temperature. 

NOTE — Dissolution of acetonitrile in water is endothermic, 


hence allow the mixing to start at ambient temperature and 
continue till it attains room temperature. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately 0.1 g of fipronil analytical standard 
of known purity into 100 ml volumetric flask. Add 50 
ml of acetonitrile and dissolve content manually by 
shaking and sonicate for 15 minutes. Allow it to attain 
room temperature and make up the volume upto the 
mark with acetonitrile. Call this as solution ‘A’. 


Pipette out 5.0 ml of solution ‘A’ into a 50 ml volumetric 
flask and make up the volume upto the mark with 
mobile phase and homogenize. Call this as solution ‘B’. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh 3.30 g of sample into a 100 ml volumetric flask. 
Add 100 ml acetonitrile with the help of volumetric 
pipette. Sonicate for 5 to 10 min. Allow it to attain 
room temperature. Filter through Whatman No. 42 
medium speed filter paper. Call this as solution ‘C’. 


Pipette out 5 ml of solution C into a 50 ml volumetric 
flask and make up the volume upto the mark with mobile 
phase and homogenize. Call this as solution ‘D’.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards ` Monthly Additions’.
